sentences.cn_text: 为了「改善生活」并减少「依赖」，财政大臣乔治·奥斯本推出了「预先求职」计划。
sentences.en_text: In order to “change lives for the better” and reduce “dependency”, George Osborne, Chancellor of the Exchequer, introduced the “upfront work search” scheme.

sentences.cn_text: 只有失业者携带简历来到就业中心、注册在线求职并开始寻找工作，才有资格领取福利——而且应每周报告而非每两周报告。
sentences.en_text: Only if the jobless arrive at the jobcentre with a CV, register for online job search, and start looking for work will they be eligible for benefit — and then they should report weekly rather than fortnightly.

sentences.cn_text: 还有什么能比这更合理呢？
sentences.en_text: What could be more reasonable?

sentences.cn_text: 更多表面上的合理性紧随其后。
sentences.en_text: More apparent reasonableness followed.

sentences.cn_text: 现在领取求职者津贴需要等待七天。
sentences.en_text: There will now be a seven-day wait for the jobseeker’s allowance.

sentences.cn_text: 「最初的几天应该用来找工作，而不是去登记领取福利，」他声称。
sentences.en_text: “Those first few days should be spent looking for work, not looking to sign on,” he claimed.

sentences.cn_text: 「我们做这些事情是因为我们知道它们能帮助人们避免依赖福利，并帮助那些领取福利的人更快找到工作。」帮助？
sentences.en_text: “We’re doing these things because we know they help people stay off benefits and help those on benefits get into work faster.” Help?

sentences.cn_text: 真的吗？
sentences.en_text: Really?

sentences.cn_text: 初听之下，这是一位关心社会的财政大臣，试图通过「改革」一个明显过于宽松的制度来改善生活，该制度对新失业者找工作的要求太低，并且补贴懒惰。
sentences.en_text: On first hearing, this was the socially concerned chancellor, trying to change lives for the better, complete with “reforms” to an obviously indulgent system that demands too little effort from the newly unemployed to find work, and subsidises laziness.

sentences.cn_text: 我们应当理解，驱动他的是对「根本公平」的热情——保护纳税人、控制支出、确保只有最值得的申请者才能获得福利。
sentences.en_text: What motivated him, we were to understand, was his zeal for “fundamental fairness” — protecting the taxpayer, controlling spending and ensuring that only the most deserving claimants received their benefits.

sentences.cn_text: 失业是痛苦的：你不会心里哼着歌蹦蹦跳跳地去就业中心，兴高采烈地期待通过慷慨的国家让收入翻倍。
sentences.en_text: Losing a job is hurting: you don’t skip down to the jobcentre with a song in your heart, delighted at the prospect of doubling your income from the generous state.

sentences.cn_text: 这在经济上令人恐惧，在心理上令人难堪，而且你知道支持微乎其微且极其难以获得。
sentences.en_text: It is financially terrifying, psychologically embarrassing and you know that support is minimal and extraordinarily hard to get.

sentences.cn_text: 你现在不被需要了；你现在被排除在为你的生活提供目标和结构的工作环境之外。
sentences.en_text: You are now not wanted; you are now excluded from the work environment that offers purpose and structure in your life.

sentences.cn_text: 更糟的是，用来养活自己和家人并支付账单的关键收入已经消失。
sentences.en_text: Worse, the crucial income to feed yourself and your family and pay the bills has disappeared.

sentences.cn_text: 问任何一个刚失业的人他们想要什么，答案总是：一份工作。
sentences.en_text: Ask anyone newly unemployed what they want and the answer is always: a job.

sentences.cn_text: 但在奥斯本的世界里，你的第一反应是陷入依赖——如果可能的话，永久依赖——而国家非常乐意纵容你的虚假。
sentences.en_text: But in Osborneland, your first instinct is to fall into dependency — permanent dependency if you can get it — supported by a state only too ready to indulge your falsehood.

sentences.cn_text: 就好像过去20年对求职和福利管理系统日益严格的改革从未发生过一样。
sentences.en_text: It is as though 20 years of ever-tougher reforms of the job search and benefit administration system never happened.

sentences.cn_text: 英国福利的原则不再是你可以为失业风险投保，并在灾难发生时获得无条件的支付。
sentences.en_text: The principle of British welfare is no longer that you can insure yourself against the risk of unemployment and receive unconditional payments if the disaster happens.

sentences.cn_text: 甚至「求职者津贴」这个短语本身就在重新定义失业者为「求职者」，他们没有通过缴纳国民保险而获得福利的基本权利。
sentences.en_text: Even the very phrase “jobseeker’s allowance” is about redefining the unemployed as a “jobseeker” who had no fundamental right to a benefit he or she has earned through making national insurance contributions.

sentences.cn_text: 相反，申请者获得的是有时限的「津贴」，条件是积极寻找工作；没有权利，也没有保险，每周71.70英镑，是欧盟中最不慷慨的之一。
sentences.en_text: Instead, the claimant receives a time-limited “allowance”, conditional on actively seeking a job; no entitlement and no insurance, at £71.70 a week, one of the least generous in the EU.

sentences.cn_text: 乔治·奥斯本的计划旨在____
sentences.en_text: George Osborne’s scheme was intended to ____

sentences.cn_text: 为失业者提供更便捷的福利获取途径。
sentences.en_text: provide the unemployed with easier access to benefits.

sentences.cn_text: 鼓励求职者积极参与求职。
sentences.en_text: encourage jobseekers’ active engagement in job seeking.

sentences.cn_text: 激励失业者自愿报告。
sentences.en_text: motivate the unemployed to report voluntarily.

sentences.cn_text: 保障求职者获得福利的合法权利。
sentences.en_text: guarantee jobseekers’ legitimate right to benefits.

sentences.cn_text: 短语「to sign on」（第2段）最可能的意思是____
sentences.en_text: The phrase “to sign on” (Para. 2) most probably means ____

sentences.cn_text: 在就业中心查看可获得的工作机会。
sentences.en_text: to check on the availability of jobs at the jobcentre.

sentences.cn_text: 接受政府对津贴的限制。
sentences.en_text: to accept the government’s restrictions on the allowance.

sentences.cn_text: 向政府登记领取津贴。
sentences.en_text: to register for an allowance from the government.

sentences.cn_text: 参加政府的就业培训项目。
sentences.en_text: to attend a governmental job-training program.

sentences.cn_text: 是什么促使财政大臣制定他的计划？
sentences.en_text: What promoted the chancellor to develop his scheme?

sentences.cn_text: 为所有人争取更好生活的愿望。
sentences.en_text: A desire to secure a better life for all.

sentences.cn_text: 保护失业者的热切愿望。
sentences.en_text: An eagerness to protect the unemployed.

sentences.cn_text: 对申请者慷慨相待的冲动。
sentences.en_text: An urge to be generous to the claimants.

sentences.cn_text: 确保纳税人公平的热情。
sentences.en_text: A passion to ensure fairness for taxpayers.

sentences.cn_text: 根据第3段，失业使人感到____
sentences.en_text: According to Paragraph 3, being unemployed makes one feel ____

sentences.cn_text: 不安。
sentences.en_text: uneasy.

sentences.cn_text: 愤怒。
sentences.en_text: enraged.

sentences.cn_text: 受侮辱。
sentences.en_text: insulted.

sentences.cn_text: 内疚。
sentences.en_text: guilty.

sentences.cn_text: 作者最可能同意以下哪项？
sentences.en_text: To which of the following would the author most probably agree?

sentences.cn_text: 英国福利制度纵容求职者的懒惰。
sentences.en_text: The British welfare system indulges jobseekers’ laziness.

sentences.cn_text: 奥斯本的改革将降低失业风险。
sentences.en_text: Osborne’s reforms will reduce the risk of unemployment.

sentences.cn_text: 求职者津贴满足了他们的实际需求。
sentences.en_text: The jobseekers’ allowance has met their actual needs.

sentences.cn_text: 失业救济金不应附加条件。
sentences.en_text: Unemployment benefits should not be made conditional.
